body:
A renderer is a delta, a channel carries deltas, and the quarantine (§24) exists to run
untrusted code behind a visible probation frame. All three are landed; what is missing is the
seam: today a peer's renderer lands in the pool as inert bytes and nothing notices, offers, or
mounts it. The vision doc's install-by-federation story — "she didn't send him an app; her
database told his database about it, and it stayed inert until he said yes" — is this ticket.

Design decisions, settled here with reasoning (final PR is Myk's merge — this decides an
app-arrival posture, so the recommendation is baked in rather than asked):
- An arriving renderer NEVER auto-mounts, and the channel's blessing toggle does NOT extend to
  renderers. Blessing governs name binding; mounting code that executes is a strictly wider
  grant, so it takes a separate, explicit, per-renderer act. Auto-bless must never mean
  auto-execute.
- The sync report names what arrived (renderer route + content hash, arrived-inert), and the
  same listing extends `loam federate list` (the CLI's existing reader — there is no
  `federate status` verb) and the loam_federate_status connector tool.
- The explicit act is `loam federate bless-app --channel <name> --route <route>` (flags, not
  positionals — every existing federate verb takes --channel; follow the convention): it mounts the renderer in
  the §24 probation frame, its writes sequestered to the channel's pool, served under the
  channel's prefix (the receiver names apps exactly as it names lenses).
- Dropping the channel unmounts and purges the renderer with the pool — the uninstall that
  provably takes everything and provably spares everything else.

Ordering, decided by in-repo precedent: a renderer whose schema dependency is not yet
blessed in the pool refuses at bless-app with the existing adopt-law refusal shape
(src/gateway/adopt-law.ts already refuses a renderer row whose schema export is unblessed and
handles the peer-bare-name to receiver-prefixed mapping — point the wiring at it, do not
reinvent the mapping).

Acceptance criteria:
(a) A peer's renderer delta lands in the pool and its route does NOT serve — present at the
    bytes, 404 at the door (two-sided inertness). Verify: new test
    test/federation/install-by-federation.test.ts.
(b) The sync report lists the arrived renderer by route and hash. Verify: same file.
(c) bless-app mounts it behind the probation frame; the rendered page carries the frame's
    marker; its writes land in the pool, not the primary ground. Verify: same file.
(d) The blessing toggle set true does not mount an arriving renderer (auto-bless never
    auto-executes — pinned). Verify: same file.
(e) Dropping the channel unmounts the app and purges its bytes AND a bystander channel's
    blessed app still serves (two-sided). Verify: same file.

Merge tier: MYK'S MERGE — widens what arriving data can do. The PR states the widening in one
line and carries this ticket's reasoning as the review guide.
title: Install by federation — an arriving renderer is inert until blessed
